verdicts.factCheck: The MegaEVM resource limits page, fetched this session, says in normative form that for data size, KV updates and state growth the first transaction that brings cumulative block usage to or above the block limit is still included, and that later candidates MUST be skipped before execution. Its outcomes table says a skipped transaction gets no receipt and 'may be reconsidered in a later block'. Its constants table sets TX_STATE_GROWTH_LIMIT and BLOCK_STATE_GROWTH_LIMIT to 1,000 each, and the transaction gas limit must fit a 'sequencer-configured per-transaction gas cap' with no published value. constants.rs and block/limit.rs fetched from mega-evm main and from tag v1.7.4 have equal SHA-256 hashes (900012bc... for limit.rs, f4605e54... for constants.rs). constants.rs lines 206 and 211 set both state growth limits to 1000, and limit.rs pre_execution_check returns StateGrowthLimit when block_state_growth_used >= block_state_growth_limit (lines 880 to 889). eth_getBlockByNumber on https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc returned block 32,849,640 with base fee 1,000,000 wei, gas limit 10,000,000,000 and gas used 9,338,037, and web3_clientVersion answered mega-reth/v2.3.1-4499c42. The 22.6 million gas cost of a filler was not re-measured here; it rests on cycle 19's eth_estimateGas. Nothing public states the reconsideration order, so the amplified form stays unconfirmed, as the finding itself says.
verdicts.codeCheck: No production file in src/ reads block.number, block.timestamp, block.basefee, gasleft or tx.origin. The only matches are in src/test (HooksTest.sol, NoDelegateCallTest.sol, TickMathTest.sol). unlock (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114) and take (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297) apply the same checks whichever block they land in, so a delayed call runs with the same rules. The skip happens before execution, so no partial state or transient delta is left behind. No funds move and no balance becomes unwithdrawable; the effect is a delay.
verdicts.corrections: The mechanism says a delayed call's outcome does not change. The checks and the requested amounts are the same, but a delayed swap or liquidity change runs against whatever pool price exists in the later block, so its realised amounts can differ within the caller's own price limit. This is ordinary latency and does not change severity. The finding duplicates F-042 apart from the unconfirmed queue rule; merging them is right.

clearedSpotChecks.note: battery.json and targeted.json in the work directory show ran equal to vectors with mismatchCount 0 and errors 0 for chain 143 and 4326 in both sets, and run.log records Monad/0.16.7 and mega-reth/v2.3.1-4499c42 at every bracket. clearedSpotChecks.check: Monad MONAD_NINE memory cap (8 MB per transaction, counted over the current frame and its parents). Can an ordinary account use it to make a PoolManager call of another user fail, or make the PoolManager continue after a failed sub-call?
clearedSpotChecks.note: I reran both eth_call probes on https://rpc.monad.xyz with gas 0x1ff2000: initcode 0x6001627fffe05200 (MSTORE ending at byte 8,388,608) returned 0x, and 0x600162800000520000 (ending at 8,388,640) returned 'out of gas'. The cap is per transaction, so an outside account reaches a victim's call only through a hook or token the victim chose, which is pool-creator scope. The cited revert paths in Hooks.sol, Currency.sol and CustomRevert.sol make a failed sub-call revert the whole call.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Monad PR #2667 (v0.16.6): can a compiled MLOAD or MSTORE skip a memory expansion it needs?
clearedSpotChecks.note: In emitter.cpp at v0.16.7, lines 6277 to 6312, touch_memory skips the bound check only for a non-literal offset element whose touched_memory_size is already at least read_size (read_size is at most 32 by the debug assert). The size is recorded just before the bound and expansion code runs; if is_bounded_by_bits fails, control goes to error_label and the frame ends. virtual_stack.hpp lines 217 to 225 show the size only grows. Memory never shrinks in a frame, so a later access through the same immutable element is covered. I did not re-read the jumpi fall-through handling on main that the cleared item cites.
